input.quote: (i) The Servicer will indemnify the Issuer, the Owner Trustee and the Indenture Trustee (including in its capacity as Note Paying Agent), and their officers, directors, employees and agents (each, an "Indemnified Person") for all fees, expenses, losses, claims, actions, suits, damages and liabilities (including reasonable legal fees and expenses) resulting from the Servicer's (including in its capacity as Custodian) willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence in performing its obligations under the Transaction Documents
input.rationale: Section 6.3 contains a counterparty-side indemnity running in our favour: Cellco as Servicer (and separately as Marketing Agent) indemnifies the Issuer, Owner Trustee and Indenture Trustee and their personnel for all fees, expenses, losses, claims, damages and liabilities (including reasonable legal fees) resulting from its willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, including costs of enforcing the indemnity. Section 6.3(b) supplies standard procedure (prompt notice that is not a condition unless prejudicial, Servicer/Marketing Agent may assume defence with counsel reasonably satisfactory to us, separate counsel at its cost on conflict, no settlement implying our acknowledgement without consent), and Section 6.3(c) provides survival past resignation, termination and trust termination. The indemnity is uncapped (no super-cap or fee-based ceiling) and there is no reciprocal Issuer/Depositor indemnity of the Servicer anywhere in the Agreement, so we sit at or above the preferred position on the material terms (Vendor indemnity for gross negligence/wilful misconduct plus standard procedure, with our own indemnity narrower than "narrow"). Section 7.5(c) additionally puts servicing-transition expenses on the resigning or terminated Servicer. Sub-elements short of preferred, noted only: there is no IP-infringement indemnity (atypical and commercially inapposite for a receivables securitisation with no services/deliverables licensed to us), no express standalone trigger for breach of applicable law or unauthorised disclosure of data (though Section 6.2(a) preserves liability for the Servicer's own willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, and Exhibit A privacy/data protection policies apply), and the Depositor is not itself named as an Indemnified Person. These are not material failures of the fallback, so no redline.
